environment.description: AWS Lambda deployed behind an internal ALB (scheme: internal) within a private VPC subnet. The ALB listener on port 443 is configured with mutual TLS authentication (mTLS) using a trust store sourced from an ACM Private CA hierarchy (arn:aws:acm-pca:us-east-1:XXXX:certificate-authority/ca-id). The ALB's mTLS mode is set to 'verify' (not 'passthrough'), meaning the ALB terminates the TLS handshake and REQUIRES a valid client certificate signed by the specified private CA before forwarding any request to the target Lambda. Client certificates are issued exclusively to internal service accounts via an automated PKI enrollment pipeline that binds the certificate CN to the service's IAM role session name. The ALB target group uses Lambda invoke integration. Additionally, the VPC has no internet gateway or NAT gateway — ingress is only possible via AWS PrivateLink from authorized peer VPCs whose security groups restrict egress to port 443 of the ALB's ENI. The trust store rejects certificates with CN values not matching the allow-list maintained in the CA's certificate policy template (which enumerates 5 specific internal service names).
